species.habitat_description: South African coastal dunes and sandy Namaqualand, with shallow subsurface runs in soft sand beneath vegetation.
species.geographic_description: Known near Port Nolloth; eDNA suggests a broader west-coast occurrence, but that extent remains provisional.
species.shape_description: Compact golden mole about 9 cm long with long slender foreclaws.
species.diet_prey: Insect larvae, pupae, and legless lizards.
species.behavior_1: Fossorial and digs shallow subsurface runs in soft sand.
species.behavior_2: Runs may extend 50-60 m beneath vegetation.
species.key_fact_1: Last documented in 1937 before its rediscovery.
species.key_fact_2: Soil eDNA and a matched specimen established survival after more than eight decades.
species.threats: Alluvial diamond mining, urban and industrial expansion, and coastal degradation.
species.distribution_comment: A broader west-coast occurrence inferred from eDNA remains provisional.

profile.habitat_note: Coastal dunes and sandy Namaqualand near Port Nolloth.
profile.morphology_note: Compact pale fawn animal with long slender digging foreclaws.
profile.diet_note: Consumes insect larvae and pupae plus legless lizards.
profile.behavior_note: Fossorial digger making shallow subsurface runs in soft sand.
profile.reference_summary: Critically endangered South African golden mole rediscovered through soil eDNA and a matched specimen.
